A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MDAC/BAL research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original gridworld simulations, six MuJoCo locomotion experiments, and five DeepMind Control Suite dog tasks, including repeated-run results in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 reports original experiments on the retained environments, additional Adroit manipulation tasks, and new bounding-function and X-SAC comparisons in Section 5 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: v1's evaluated MDAC variants use fixed bounding functions. v2 introduces the time-dependent successor-term function g_t in Equation 13, which gradually approaches the identity, and uses it in the longer Adroit/dog experiments. This extends one component while retaining the architecture and underlying actor-critic formulation.

E1.justification: v2 adds AdroitHandDoor-v1, AdroitHandHammer-v1, and AdroitHandPen-v1, substantially extending evaluation from locomotion to dexterous hand manipulation. The gridworld, six MuJoCo environments, and five dog tasks remain; the gridworld study moves to Appendix C.1.

E2.justification: The MuJoCo comparison expands from SAC and TD3 in v1 Figure 8 to SAC, TD3, and X-SAC in v2 Figure 5. Appendix C.2.4 supplies X-SAC results. SAC remains the comparator for the dog experiments.

E3.justification: The dog evaluation budget doubles from 5M to 10M environment steps. v2 also introduces 10M-step Adroit evaluations with a 3e-5 learning rate and a seven-value Gumbel-scale sweep for X-SAC. These substantially extend the evaluation settings; the existing MuJoCo budgets and network sizes remain.

E4.justification: v2 extends the bounding-function ablations with g_t and tests sensitivity to its relaxation timescale T1 in Appendix C.2.2. Appendix C.2.4 also examines X-SAC's scale sensitivity. The existing fixed-function, current-versus-successor bounding, and clipping diagnostics are retained.

E5.justification: The reported dog experiment run count decreases from 30 to 10. Corresponding MuJoCo appendix captions change the stated shading from minimum–maximum values in v1 to 25th–75th percentiles in v2. IQM scores and pointwise 95% stratified-bootstrap confidence reporting remain.

E6.justification: v2 adds Adroit, X-SAC, and scheduling/sensitivity results and replaces the dog results under the longer, scheduled-bounding setting. Figures 6–7 report advantages for MDAC on Adroit Pen and dog walk, alongside degradation of both methods on Door. Figure 5 reports X-SAC below the other MuJoCo methods. The dog differences represent revised experimental conditions.

T1.justification: Corollary 1 and Appendix B.7 add an explicit entropy-based sufficient condition for reducing the entropy-related error. Much of its supporting discussion already appears in v1 Section 4.3. The principal convergence and error-bound results are retained: v1 Theorem 1 becomes Appendix Theorem B.2, and Theorem 2 becomes Proposition 2.

C1.justification: The main claims about MDAC, bounded advantages, convergence, and baseline performance remain. v2's conclusion adds the substantive recommendation that successor-term bounding should gradually approach the identity during training.

C2.justification: v2 explains that successor-term bounding is particularly beneficial when the current policy is overly deterministic relative to the optimum, potentially amplifying incorrect action gaps. It also motivates gradually relaxing the bound. v1 discusses the convergence/error-reduction tradeoff more generally. The three stated limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a software-version/license table, the X-SAC implementation source, and explicit scheduling and sweep parameters. The core MDAC hyperparameters and the V100/8-CPU, approximately eight-hour runtime disclosure are retained. The version table supplies additional documentation without establishing changes to previously used software.

R1.justification: v2 adds Garg et al. (2023) on Extreme Q-learning, Zhu et al. (2023) on Tsallis-based Munchausen RL, and Rajeswaran et al. (2018) for Adroit. It modestly expands discussion beyond KL/entropy regularization and broadens the introductory performance-gap framing, while retaining the original mirror-descent positioning.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the theoretical and experimental narrative. The general convergence theorem and extended error discussion move into Appendices B.4 and B.7, while the main analysis centers on propositions and Corollary 1. The gridworld study moves from Section 5.1 to Appendix C.1, and the experimental appendix gains dedicated subsections.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column main-text layout and extensively rearranges displays. Bounding analyses are grouped into Figure 4, the gridworld diagram and results are combined in Figure 8, and new scheduling, sensitivity, X-SAC, and Adroit displays are introduced. A software table is added and existing plots are redrawn with revised captions and shading.

improvement.justification: The scheduling study supplies practical guidance absent from v1, while Adroit and longer evaluations broaden empirical support. The explicit entropy condition and software-version disclosures improve precision and reproducibility. These are useful extensions of v1's existing theoretical and experimental foundation. The dog evaluation trades 30 runs for 10, tempering the gain in experimental strength and supporting a limited net improvement.
